title: Risk-Controlled Applicability Set Retrieval (RCASR) for Regulation-Grounded Construction-Site Visual Screening — code, frozen configurations, analysis plans and aggregate results (ARGus)
description: Code and evaluation artifacts for Risk-Controlled Applicability Set Retrieval (RCASR), accompanying the manuscript "Risk-Controlled Applicability Set Retrieval for Regulation-Grounded Construction-Site Visual Screening". Screening a site photograph against a regulation library first requires deciding which provisions apply. RCASR frames this as set prediction under asymmetric miss/exposure cost: it re-weights a retrieval prior by the probability that each provision's compiled subject and state conditions hold, computed from token-level posteriors over 131 rule-agnostic visual atoms with abstention, and selects a set at a target mean width or under conformal risk control. On 346 photographs from 48 sites under a 42-provision regime, with site-grouped cross-fitting, recorded-violation recall at a matched mean width of three rose from 0.515 (BM25) to 0.709. A pre-specified width-two arm kept BM25's width-three recall while cutting false alarms per image from 1.28 to 1.00. Frozen before public scoring, RCASR raised ConstructionSite-10k violation detection for harness use from 0.08 to 0.80 and for PPE from 0.43 to 0.67. The configuration runs on a quadruped patrol robot. Release v2.1.0 adds a runner that applies the robot's frozen configuration to any image, a guide that screens ConstructionSite-10k test images fetched with the user's own gated access and compares the result with the released selection, and 20 further sample images anonymised by an audited Gaussian blur. Release v2.0.0 added the RCASR code, the frozen runtime configurations, the pre-specified analysis plans, SHA-256 input snapshots and the aggregate results behind every table, on top of the ARGus screening framework of the earlier study (v1.x), whose code, provision library, prompts, sample images, aggregate results and online supplement are retained. Site imagery, gold annotations and per-pair model outputs are not included; they are available from the corresponding author under a data-use agreement.
